description.p: Blockwork lets you build keyboard and mouse macros by snapping blocks together, without writing any code. Record your input and turn it into editable blocks, or assemble a sequence by hand, then play it back with a global hotkey.

ul.li: Record keyboard and mouse input, including mouse movement
Loops, If / If-Else blocks, variables, and operators
Wait blocks with randomized timing
Reusable custom blocks with custom colors
Global hotkeys to start and stop macros
Triggers and schedules: text expansion, windows, files, apps, idle time, USB devices and cron
Screen, image and window blocks, including text recognition
File, web, shell and dialog blocks, with permissions for shared macros

p.em: Recording input and hotkeys requires your user to be in the input group. See the Help link for setup steps.

Choosing how Blockwork looks and starts

ul.li: Report a community pack, or someone else's comment on it, from its page in the Block library.
The Text block spaces keystrokes 0.5 ms apart on Windows and macOS too, as it already did on Linux, so fast typing doesn't drop or merge characters.
Date and time format patterns such as MMM d are no longer translated, so dates in the run log show the right format in every language.

Optional typing speed on the Text block: wait per character, or give the whole text a total time divided evenly across it. Without it, typing runs at the normal input speed (Linux keeps a small 0.5 ms built-in gap).
Search blocks also finds blocks by the words on them (labels and dropdown choices, such as "is pressed"), in any word order, and still finds something when a word has a typo.
Windows: two-finger touchpad scrolling and pinch zoom on the canvas and palette follow the fingers like on Linux, instead of gliding behind each small step.
Blocks stay under the pointer while branches resize; bracket shapes update in the same frame as a drop.
Blocks keep their blue outline when a drag ends.
Drag previews line up when moving blocks between branches of a bracket block.
Details opens for custom blocks inside fields, including If conditions.
A trigger that fires again while its macro is still running (a hotkey toggle around a forever loop) now sees the variables the running strands set, so a second press can switch the toggle off.
The portable Windows zip unzips to one Blockwork folder that runs on a clean install.
The Windows updater downloads the installer for the PC's own architecture, so Windows on Arm updates to the arm64 build.
Number fields (such as the typing speed's milliseconds or the numbers in Add and Divide) no longer show the bigger text box button, since they can't hold more than one line.
The Minimize button now shows the correct icon.

description.p: A large feature release: macros can now react to what happens on the computer and see the screen.

ul.li: Triggers for typed abbreviations, windows, files, apps, idle time, network, USB devices, schedules and webhooks, with pickers for times and schedules
Screen, image, text recognition and window blocks, with a screen picker in the editor
File, web, shell, notification and dialog blocks
Error handling, a debugger with breakpoints, and an emergency stop hotkey
Global variables, secrets kept in the system keyring, and macros that run other macros
Browser blocks through the new Blockwork browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox
A searchable macro library, shareable bundles and block packs, with a permission review on import
A community block library to browse, install and publish block packs
Text boxes with several lines, and a stop block for the whole macro, one strand or the others
A translatable interface, a command line, and starter templates
Smooth animations and scrolling, with an animation speed setting from instant to slow

description.p: Blockwork is now available as a Flatpak, and runs as a background daemon with a separate editor window.
The project has moved to the Blockworked organization on GitHub.
Blockwork can now update itself on macOS.
Custom blocks were reworked and can now be given their own colors. The sidebar shows the correct operator type.
The app is now called Blockwork, with a new logo and a smoother block editor with better pan, zoom, and dragging.

ul.li: Loops, booleans, and If / If-Else blocks
Time and date blocks, app open and quit blocks, and a battery event
Mouse movement recording
A system tray icon

description.p: Macros are now built in a Scratch-like block editor. Variables show a live preview of their value, and new operators include Join, Random, and text blocks.
Hotkeys no longer stop working after switching windows with Alt+Tab.
Settings and macros are stored in a new config directory layout.
Global hotkeys can now be recorded, macros can be force-quit, and playback timing is more precise. Wait blocks accept fractional seconds and an optional random variance.
The run-script block can now run any command, and you are warned if your user is not in the input group.
Added input recording, custom hotkey settings, undo and redo, comments, and relative mouse movement. Large macros are faster to edit.
